extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report publishing President Roosevelt's wartime address (Oct. 1942) together with Navy communiqués and battlefield reporting; intended to inform the general public about manpower policy, draft proposals, production, and naval actions in the Solomons. Covers policy objectives, operational details, and public reassurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall war objective – destroy enemy military power
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of today is clear and realistic. It is to destroy completely the military power of Germany, Italy, and Japan, to taper such good purpose that their threat against us and all the other United Nations cannot be revived a generation hence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as the principal strategic aim guiding military and postwar policy; it implies comprehensive defeat of enemy armed forces and measures to prevent future revival of their military power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-propaganda and public resilience (war of nerves)
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest defense against such propaganda is the common sense of the common people — and that defense is prevailing. The 'war of nerves' against the United Nations is now turning into a boomerang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes reliance on informed public judgment as the primary countermeasure to enemy psychological operations; notes Nazi propaganda is on the defensive and beginning to apologize to its own people. Implied guidance: maintain credible information, public morale, and vigilance against fifth-column influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and documentation of atrocities; judicial process for leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: As each of these criminal deeds is committed, it is being carefully investigated; and the evidence is being relentlessly piled up for the future purposes of justice. The ring leaders and their brutal henchmen must be named, and apprehended, and tried in accordance with the judicial processes of criminal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for systematic collection of evidence and legal prosecution of responsible individuals rather than mass reprisals; stresses legal procedures and accountability as postwar policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major objectives of a sound manpower policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The major objectives of a sound manpower policy are: First, to select and train men of the highest fighting efficiency needed for our armed forces in the achievement of victory over our enemies in combat. Second, to man our war industries and farms with the workers needed to produce the arms and munitions and food required by ourselves and our fighting Allies to win this war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompanying measures include stopping unnecessary transfer of workers between war jobs, preventing employers from 'stealing' labor from each other, using older men, handicapped people, more women, and even grown boys and girls where reasonable, training new personnel for essential war work, and stopping wastage of labor in non-essential activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manpower mobilization measures and anti-waste practices
rubrics_metrics.description: To do this we shall be compelled to stop workers from moving from one war job to another as a matter of personal preference; to stop employers from stealing labor from each other; to use older men, and handicapped people, and more women, and even grown boys and girls, wherever possible and reasonable, to replace men of military age and fitness; to train new personnel for essential war work; and to stop the wastage of labor in all non-essential activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific proposals and examples: enlist high school students to help harvest with no harm to education, encourage community ingenuity and cooperation on farms, use the U.S. Employment Service network to match skills to essential jobs, and consider legislation if volunteer efforts prove insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft-age adjustment and criteria for overseas combat units
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our combat units that go overseas must consist of young, strong men who have had thorough training. A division that has an average age of twenty-three or twenty-four is a better fighting unit than one which has an average age of thirty or thirty-four. Therefore, I believe that it will be necessary to lower the present minimum age limit for selective service from twenty years down to eighteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument links unit fighting efficiency and casualty reduction to age and training; legislative action (lowering draft age to 18) is presented as inevitable and necessary to speed victory and reduce casualties. Congressional leaders are cited as likely to support hearings/legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of training, equipment, and medical care for service members
rubrics_metrics.description: Sons in the services are receiving 'the best possible training, equipment and medical care.' Good training will save many, many lives in battle; the highest rate of casualties is always suffered by units comprised of inadequately trained men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance to families and the public that investment in training and care directly reduces battlefield casualties; implies prioritizing training quality in manpower policy and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture as integral to war production and mobilization of farm labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Every farmer in the land must realize fully that his production is part of War production, and that he is regarded by the nation as essential to victory. The people of his community must use ingenuity and cooperative effort to produce crops and livestock and dairy products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes community-based solutions to farm labor shortages (e.g., turning whole high-school classes out to harvest perishable crops), potential need for new legislation if volunteer efforts do not suffice, and local coordination to keep production up or increased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping, merchant marine service, and protection of transports
rubrics_metrics.description: In expanding our shipping, we have had to enlist many thousands of men for our merchant marine. These men are serving magnificently. Screening groups of Allied cruisers and destroyers were placed on both sides of Savo Island to guard the western entrances to the transport area; additional screening forces were stationed near transports to provide close coverage within the harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criteria for protecting convoy/transport operations: place screening groups to guard approaches, station destroyers for close coverage inside harbor areas, and reallocate ships (made possible by new ship construction) to offset losses. Emphasizes shipbuilding and merchant marine recruitment as part of transportation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic necessity of opening other offensives and operational security
rubrics_metrics.description: Many major decisions of strategy have been made. One of them... relates to the necessity of diverting enemy forces from Russia and China to other theaters of war by new offensives against Germany and Japan. An announcement of how these offensives are to be launched, and, when, and where, cannot be broadcast over the radio at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: conduct offensives to relieve allied fronts; maintain operational security by withholding timing/locations; plan and coordinate allied operations rather than publicizing sensitive details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and act on allied unity and coordinated planning
rubrics_metrics.description: We are united in seeking the objective in common with representatives of Russia, China, the Netherlands, Poland, Norway, the British Dominions, and other nations working in the common cause. The chiefs of this staff meet and confer regularly with representatives of the British joint staff, and with representatives of the Navy, Army and Air commanders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes regular allied coordination at high levels; unity of effort is presented as essential to strategic decisions and successful operations. Implied standard: maintain and reinforce multinational cooperation and planning.
